<description>
**Problem:** Block and undo writers buffer serialized data, then rely on the `BufferedWriter` destructor to write the remaining bytes.
`fwrite()` can report fewer bytes written than requested after a local storage error, e.g., if the filesystem fills up while a block is being written (my 1 TB benchmarking servers have recently been filling up, so I've been seeing these failures more often).
`AutoFile::write_buffer()` converts that result into an exception, and because the destructor is implicitly non-throwing, the exception invokes `std::terminate`.
Calling `flush()` before destruction is insufficient on its own because a failed flush leaves the same bytes pending, so the destructor retries the write while the original exception unwinds.

I introduced this bug in #31551 when adding `BufferedWriter`.

I’d update the **Fix** section to include `discard()` and describe exactly what the destructor checks. The problem statement and reproducer can stay as written.

**Fix:** Block and undo writers now flush explicitly before destruction.
If serialization or writing throws `std::ios_base::failure`, they discard any pending bytes, log the error, close the file, and request shutdown through the existing fatal-error path.
`BufferedWriter` clears the pending byte count before writing because the stream may obfuscate the bytes in place and a short write may already have put some of them on disk, making a retry unsafe.
The destructor uses `Assume` to check that no bytes are pending before attempting a fallback flush.
`flush()` continues to propagate exceptions, and `AutoFile` remains unchanged.

Manual write-error reproducer

Force the error path in `AutoFile::write_buffer()`:

```sh
sed -i '' '/^.*AutoFile::write_buffer(/,/^}/s/!= src.size()/!= 0/' src/streams.cpp
cmake -B build && cmake --build build -j5 && build/bin/bitcoind -regtest -datadir="$(mktemp -d)"; echo "exit=$?"
```

Before this change, implicit flushing invokes `std::terminate`:

[quoted text omitted]
With this change, `bitcoind` logs the write failure, then completes normal shutdown and exits with status 1:

[quoted text omitted]
</description>

Correct, and I think this assumption holds. If serializing one of our valid C++ structs (like a block) failed, it seems like a severe internal bug, and I think crashing here is better. Recall that your suggested patch will also continue to crash on non-io exceptions after the first buffered byte. Also, your patch will continue to crash if there was an interrupt (somewhere else due to an io error) and then the flush failed.

No objection, just wondering what should be in scope and what should be better ignored.
